clue.text: Penny steered badly when driven round the bend and …

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

indicators.note: steered badly means the letters of that word are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A driver who steers poorly ends up going round a bend, with the sentence carried on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 5 across. 'badly' gives ESTERED. 'Round the bend' looks like part of the driving picture, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being driven round the bend is a British idiom for being annoyed to distraction, which is what being nagged does to you.

clue.text: Brave uncle

definitions.meaning: a brave is a Native American warrior
uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, the person who takes goods in pawn

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective but is a noun. Strictly the pawnbroker is the pawnee, the one with whom goods are pawned, in legal use.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawnee names a Native American people of Nebraska and, in law, the person receiving a pledge, the pawnbroker.

clue.text: Mean to irritate youth leader

parts.note: to sting is to irritate, as a remark stings

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A youth leader may mean to annoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb but is the adjective tight-fisted; 'youth leader' gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy and mean both describe someone unwilling to spend or give money.

clue.text: Former draughtsman in the Treasury

parts.note: ex means former
a draughtsman is a piece in the game of draughts, also called a checker or chequer

explanation.surface: A retired technical drawer works in the Treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draughtsman' suggests someone drawing plans, but is a draughts counter, a CHEQUER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the British government department in charge of public revenue, the Treasury.

clue.text: Greek scholar in Muse's former quarters

parts.note: Erato is the Muse of lyric poetry
then means at a former time
E and S, east and south, are two of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek scholar living in rooms that once belonged to a Muse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like lodgings but gives two compass points, E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Eratosthenes was the Greek scholar of Alexandria who measured the earth's circumference.

clue.text: … pressure has Don also going round the bend

indicators.note: the word for Don goes round, enclosing the letter that stands for the bend

parts.note: to don clothes is to dress
a U-bend is shaped like the letter U, so the bend gives U

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 across: a man called Don is also being driven mad by pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a man's name but is the verb to put on clothes. 'going round' puts DRESS round U, the U-bend of plumbing; 'also' just links back to 1 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is compulsion by threats or force, a form of pressure put on someone to act.

clue.text: Awfully cruel medical condition

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done in a terrible way, so the letters of cruel are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadfully harsh illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges CRUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is an open sore, a medical condition of skin or stomach lining.

clue.text: Trace ten gone astray in the interval

indicators.note: gone astray means wandered off course, so the letters of trace and ten are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten people go missing during the break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone astray' rearranges TRACE and TEN together.
explanation.definitionFit: An entr'acte is the interval between two acts of a play, or music played then.

clue.text: Throw up in pigpen that's extendable

indicators.note: the vomiting word goes in the pig's pen

parts.note: a sty is a pigpen
to retch is to throw up or try to

explanation.surface: Being sick in a pigsty, which is somehow elastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' looks like tossing something upward, but it means being sick; 'in' does the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretchy can be pulled out longer, so it is extendable.

clue.text: Bird to move slowly? What about that?

indicators.note: the word What goes about, surrounding the verb for creeping along

parts.note: taken as written
to inch is to move slowly, a little at a time

explanation.surface: Someone asks, puzzled, what is meant by a bird that moves slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the moving word in What; the question marks and 'that' are just the surface's chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: The whinchat is a small brown songbird of open country, related to the stonechat.

clue.text: Cortes prepared duck

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters of Cortes are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: The conquistador Cortes cooks a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges CORTES; Cortes was the Spanish conqueror of Mexico, a name chosen for its handy letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck found off northern coasts.

clue.text: Rate the Torah badly in private discussion

indicators.note: badly here means poorly arranged, so the letters of rate, the and Torah are shuffled

explanation.surface: Giving the Torah a poor review during a private talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges RATE, THE and TORAH together.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart-to-heart is a frank, intimate conversation between two people.

clue.text: Old comic welcomed on the golf course

definitions.meaning: a famous British boys' comic paper of the 1950s and 60s
on a golf course a score of two under par on a hole is a cheering result for any player

explanation.surface: A veteran comedian is warmly received at a golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old comic' reads as an elderly comedian, but it is a British comic paper, Eagle, famous for Dan Dare.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagle names both the old comic paper and the golf score two strokes under par, which golfers delight in.

clue.text: Lose a sense of proportion when soldiers tuck into ham

indicators.note: the soldiers tuck into, going inside, the word for hamming it up

parts.note: to ham is to overact on stage
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a regular crossword abbreviation for soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers eating ham get carried away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' looks like eating, and 'ham' like the food; in fact ham is the verb, as in a hammy actor.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreact is to respond more strongly than a situation warrants, losing all sense of proportion.

clue.text: Bachelor says bed companion is sweet

parts.note: to utter is to say, so says gives utters
a cot is a small bed
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A single man declares that the person sharing his bed is lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed companion' reads as a lover, but is two pieces; the Companion of Honour is a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard, brittle confection of butter and brown sugar, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Boat in a river in Canada

indicators.note: a and the river go in, inside the abbreviation for Canada

parts.note: the Tamar is the river dividing Devon and Cornwall in England

explanation.surface: A boat on a river in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does the placing, splitting the Canada abbreviation after its second letter. The Tamar is an English river, not Canadian.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a boat with two parallel hulls.

clue.text: Confine to bed in A&E? That's novel!

indicators.note: the confining word and bed go in, inside A and E

parts.note: A and E taken as the two letters
to dam is to confine water
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hospital emergency department confining a patient to bed: how new!
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like an exclamation meaning new, but is a noun: George Eliot's novel. A&E is the British hospital accident and emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Bede is the 1859 novel by George Eliot.

clue.text: Bridge opponents demand round of coffee

parts.note: in bridge East and South sit on opposing sides
to press is to demand urgently
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Bridge players insist on buying the next round of coffees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round of coffee' looks like a drinks order; 'round' gives O and 'of' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Is East in time for puzzle?

indicators.note: Is and the word for East go in, inside the word for a time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
taken as written
the Orient is the East

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the east is on time, as a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does the placing; 'puzzle' looks like a noun but is the verb, to confuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To disorientate someone is to confuse them, which is what a puzzle does as a verb.

clue.text: Sister caught with one old ambassador

parts.note: a sister is a nun
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nun is caught with a former envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is a papal ambassador to a foreign government.

clue.text: Ridicule the regional tableware

parts.note: to tease is to make fun of, ridicule
in northern English dialect the is shortened to t'

explanation.surface: Mocking the local crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire speech 'the' is shortened to t', as in 'down t'pit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea set is a matching group of cups, saucers and pot, which is tableware.

clue.text: Search through swamp in North Africa

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in North Africa rather than a synonym

indicators.note: the search word goes through the swamp word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a marsh is a swamp
to rake is to search thoroughly, as through papers

explanation.surface: Someone combs a North African swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' does the placing; the definition gives a location rather than a synonym, which is fair for a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrakesh is a historic city of Morocco, so it lies in North Africa.

clue.text: Give consent in Gretna Green

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run Gretna Green

explanation.surface: Agreeing to marry at Gretna Green.
explanation.walkthrough: Gretna Green is a Scottish village famous for runaway weddings, apt for consent.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to consent, as couples do when they marry.

clue.text: Vermin in doctor's practice

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
use and practice both mean customary exercise of something

explanation.surface: Rats or mice have got into the surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor's practice' looks like one phrase, a surgery, but it is two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Mice are small rodents commonly classed as household pests or vermin.

clue.text: Guarantee rebuke when scratching head

indicators.note: scratching here means striking out, so the first letter of the rebuke word is removed

parts.note: to censure is to rebuke

explanation.surface: A promise made while scolding someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching head' looks like puzzlement, but means scratch out the head letter: CENSURE loses its C.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to make certain, to guarantee that something happens.

clue.text: Accommodation for pub fittings

parts.note: a bar is a pub
racks are fittings for holding things

explanation.surface: Asking where the fixtures and fittings of a pub can be stored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pub fittings' reads as one phrase, but BAR and RACKS are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracks are buildings housing soldiers, a form of accommodation.

clue.text: Worn down journalist travelled inside

indicators.note: the travel word goes inside the abbreviation for a newspaper editor

parts.note: ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist
rode means travelled, as on horseback or a bus

explanation.surface: A weary reporter has been doing the rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' does the placing; 'journalist' is almost always the editor in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Eroded means gradually worn away, as rock is by water or wind.

clue.text: Catch the eye of porter grabbing joiner

indicators.note: the beer word grabs, holding inside it, the joining word

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, like stout
and is a conjunction, a word that joins

explanation.surface: Getting a porter's attention by grabbing a carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' and 'joiner' look like jobs: one is the beer STOUT, the other the conjunction AND.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand out is to be conspicuous, to catch the eye among others.
